title: Hash maps
summary: Key lookup is O(1) on average and O(n) when every key collides.

parts.rule: Store key to value under a hash of the key. Average get, put, and delete are O(1). Worst case is O(n) when every key lands in one bucket. Say average unless the interviewer asks for worst case, and name a collision story if pressed.
parts.why: Counting, grouping, and "have I seen this" are the default interview moves. People claim O(1) without the average caveat, or they pick a map when an array index already is the key. The failure mode is a silent O(n) scan disguised as a lookup, or a map used where a boolean array of size 26 would do.

body:
Rule. Store key to value under a hash of the key. Average get, put, and delete are O(1). Worst case is O(n) when every key lands in one bucket. Say average unless the interviewer asks for worst case, and name a collision story if pressed.

Why it matters. Counting, grouping, and "have I seen this" are the default interview moves. People claim O(1) without the average caveat, or they pick a map when an array index already is the key. The failure mode is a silent O(n) scan disguised as a lookup, or a map used where a boolean array of size 26 would do.

Worked example. Count frequencies in [3, 1, 3, 2, 1, 3]. Start with empty map. See 3 → {3:1}. See 1 → {3:1, 1:1}. See 3 → {3:2, 1:1}. See 2 → {3:2, 1:1, 2:1}. See 1 → {3:2, 1:2, 2:1}. See 3 → {3:3, 1:2, 2:1}. Six operations, each a hash probe. Answer: 3 appears three times. Now find the first unique: scan again; 2 has count 1, return index of 2. Contrast: if keys were lowercase letters only, a length-26 array indexed by ord(c)-ord("a") would skip hashing entirely and still give O(1) per character.

When to use. Use a hash map for frequency counts, adjacency for sparse graphs, memo tables, and membership when keys are arbitrary. Use it when you need average-case constant lookup and n is large enough that a linear scan hurts. Use an ordered map only when the prompt needs sorted keys.

When to refuse. Refuse a hash map when keys are dense small integers and an array index is enough. Refuse claiming worst-case O(1) without a perfect hash or tree map. Refuse hashing a mutable object that can change after insert. Refuse a map as the whole design when the access pattern is sequential scan of every entry every time.
